{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0) to account for bearish market pressure.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes by applying a 10-15% dampening factor to the immediate next period.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates > ±15% from recent 5-day average, adjust toward the average.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (sentiment ≈ 0) to avoid overconfidence.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce volatility in the later half (days 20-30) to reflect diminishing momentum and market stabilization.",
    "When sentiment shows a clear upward trend (e.g., >0.5), slightly increase forecast slope to reflect bullish momentum, but cap at 5% above recent peak.",
    "If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast by 5-10% to avoid overestimating upward momentum."
  ]
}
